documents.unit: Office of the General Counsel (Academic Misconduct Policy 4.1.7)
documents.title: Academic Misconduct Policy
documents.summary: A general academic misconduct policy that lists 'unauthorized use of artificial intelligence' as one form of cheating. It sets no rules on what AI use is allowed and leaves authorization to instructors and course policies.
documents.stance_why: The only AI text is the bullet 'unauthorized use of artificial intelligence' under cheating. It bans AI only when unauthorized and never says who authorizes it or what is authorized, so the document sets no AI stance itself and defers to others (delegates), rather than prohibit or restrict.

units.why: The bullet lists 'unauthorized use of artificial intelligence' as a form of cheating, i.e. academic misconduct subject to disciplinary action, so P36 (unauthorized AI as misconduct) fits; it is addressed to students (the policy binds 'any student') and applies to misconduct generally, so the phase is when-misuse. It is not P06 because it states no fallback for silent syllabi, and not P04 because it does not say who decides.
units.policy: Unauthorized use of artificial intelligence is cheating, a form of academic misconduct for which students are subject to disciplinary action.

notes: Single thin AI mention. Document is general misconduct policy; non-AI provisions (appeals, course-policy violations, syllabus pointer) were not coded as they say nothing about AI.
